extraction.Name: Lucy Patton
extraction.Post Office Address: Pine Ridge, care of the Holy Rosary Mission, South Dakota
extraction.Refused/Protested: did not want the patent in fee to her 160 acre allotment, when it was issued, April 13, 1818, for she did not want to pay taxes; but the Indian Agency informed her that, if she did not take care of it, the land would be assessed for taxes, for which it would later be sold; so she accepted the patent in fee
extraction.Sold/Mortgaged: in 1918, she sold her allotment to Harry Evans, for $600.00 cash
extraction.Occupation/Income: she sews for the Holy Rosary Mission, which her only source of income
extraction.NOTES: mentally competent; has very poor health; has no one to support but herself; she never sold her land for any debts incurred before receiving the patent in fee; has never received any help from the County, State nor the United States Government; she considers she received a very poor price for her land; document No. 6802; subscribed and sworn December 17, 1928; fee patent date as stated in document reads April 13, 1818, likely a transcription error for 1918 | TASK 5 BULK ALLOTMENT RECOVERY 2026-04-29: Sonnet text-extraction captured the allotment number from the source page header but classified it in NOTES as a 'document number' / 'Document No.' / 'No. NNNN' instead of placing it in the structured Allotment number field. The hypothesis that these document/file references are actually allotment numbers was confirmed via BLM cross-reference (exemplars: Eugene Means 2249, Lucy Patton 6802). This patch corrects 48 records via bulk regex extraction from NOTES with user-supervised review of every HIGH-confidence proposal.

recovery_notes.rationale: Source page header contained 'No. NNNN' which Sonnet captured in NOTES as 'document number' rather than placing in structured Allotment field. Hypothesis confirmed via BLM cross-reference.
